summary: Stanley Lombardo works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at De La Salle High School, Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1976 to 2014.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Stanley Weinstein studied at Komazawa University, the University of Tokyo, and Harvard, learning under Gyokusen Hosaka, Kodo Sawaki, and Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS, London, and Yale University.

Stanley Wolpert was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as assistant, associate professor, and department chair at the University of California, Los Angeles (1959–2002).
Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 1965–1970, where he studied under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (circa 2002–2009) and has held posts at Copenhagen, Washington, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Stockholm under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, and studied under David F. Germano, later holding posts at Berkeley, Virginia, and Gävle.

Stefan Mario Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Free University of Berlin, later holding posts at Berlin, the University of Heidelberg, and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and director at the University of Groningen circa 2013–2020 and took up a post at SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Sichuan University, and Leiden University under mentors including Alfredo Cadonna and Tilmann Vetter, later holding appointments at Soka, Ca' Foscari, and Oxford.

Steffen Döll specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University, and later held positions at Kyoto, Munich, Seikei University, Marburg, and the University of Hamburg.

Stella Kramrisch was an Indology and art history scholar who studied under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski at the University of Vienna. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, New York University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

Sten Konow was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at Oslo, Berlin, and Halle under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel, holding posts at Oslo, the Prussian State Library, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Hamburg.

Stephan Kigensan Licha specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London by 2012 and held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo.

Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson, served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1972–1980), and held a post at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry, learning under Thich Nhat Hanh and Joanna Macy, and was a professor at the University of Vermont (1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar of Tibetology who conducted her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist. She completed her doctoral work at Yale University under Stanley Insler and Warren Cowgill, and held academic posts at Harvard University and the University of California, Los Angeles.

Stephen Addiss specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Harvard, Mannes, The New School, and Michigan, and held professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013), alongside curatorial roles.

Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Goenka, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, Kusan Sunim, and Gombrich. He held positions at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, Songgwangsa, Sharpham College, and Bodhi College.
